title: Pre-SOW Discovery & Scoping Questionnaire
lede: The companion instrument to the post-SOW readiness survey, fielded before signature. Its job is not readiness — it is scope accuracy. Every answer either sizes the SOW or becomes a written assumption that protects it, and every unanswered question is a change order waiting to happen.

questions.text: Full name
Job title and department
What is your role in this evaluation?
Have you been through a platform migration like this before?
questions.logic: A first-time migration team needs more hand-holding hours than an experienced one. This is an effort input, not a judgment, and it belongs in the estimate.

questions.text: What is prompting this change now?
What happens if nothing changes in the next twelve months? (select all that apply)
options: Growth or a new site is blocked
questions.logic: "Nothing material" is the most useful answer this question produces. It tells you the deal has no compelling event and the SOW will sit unsigned regardless of how good it is.

questions.text: Incumbent contract end date and notice-of-termination window
Is there a hard date this must be live by?
Rank these outcomes by priority.
What have you already tried, and why did it not resolve this?
questions.logic: Surfaces a failed prior implementation, an abandoned internal project, or a competitor already in the account. All three change how you scope and how you price.

questions.text: Primary voice platform today
Contact center platform today, if different
Sites: ____  ·  Countries: ____  ·  Total employees: ____  ·  Employees needing a phone: ____
Contact center agents: ____  ·  Supervisors: ____  ·  Administrators: ____
What is on-premise today?
Who supports voice today?
The customer's documentation of existing call flows and routing is accurate and current.
questions.logic: Direct multiplier on discovery hours. A score of 2 or below means you are reverse-engineering the current state from the platform itself, which is billable work that has to be in the estimate rather than absorbed.

questions.text: Who owns and maintains the call-flow and routing documentation?
questions.logic: Names the owner behind the P2.7 accuracy score. "Tribal knowledge" or "none" means discovery is reverse-engineering, not review — price it. Ask the owner to attach the flow docs (＋ Note / attachment) so they land in the project folder.

questions.text: Documented call flows: ____ · Routing/IVR diagrams available: ____
questions.logic: Current-state documentation count, distinct from the total distinct flows sized in P7.1 — the gap between them is undocumented flow you will have to discover.

questions.text: Zoom Phone users: ____  ·  Common-area or shared devices: ____  ·  Contact center agents: ____  ·  Supervisors needing a license: ____
questions.logic: Target Zoom licensing — what to buy. May differ from the current-state counts in P2.3/P2.4 (the incumbent). Enter the seats to license on Zoom; leave 0 where a product is not in scope.

questions.text: Which channels at go-live?
Monthly volume — Voice: ____  ·  Digital (all channels): ____  ·  Outbound attempts: ____
Peak concurrency — Inbound voice: ____  ·  Digital conversations: ____  ·  Logged-in agents: ____
questions.logic: Enter whole numbers — the maximum handled at the same time during your busiest interval, not daily totals. Inbound voice = concurrent calls; Digital = concurrent chat/email/SMS; Logged-in agents = peak agents active at once. A best estimate is fine — record how you got it in P3.5.

questions.text: How did you arrive at those concurrency figures? (select all that apply — e.g. measured for voice, estimated for digital)
options: Derived from Erlang or WFM modelling
questions.logic: The highest-leverage question in the instrument. Anything below "measured" means the sizing assumption clause goes into the SOW verbatim — see section 4.

questions.text: Expected growth over 24 months:
How do you want to cut over?
questions.logic: The single largest driver of professional services effort in the whole instrument. Extended coexistence means hybrid routing, dual number estates, and a dual-run cost the customer has usually not budgeted for. Price it explicitly or exclude it explicitly.

questions.text: CRM and service systems in scope
Clinical, vertical and operational systems in scope
What do you expect each selected system to require?
questions.logic: Expectation-setting question as much as a scoping one. A prospect who assumes out-of-box for a custom EHR has priced the project wrong in their own head, and finding that out pre-proposal is far cheaper than finding it out at the pricing review.

questions.text: Do you have API access and a named internal owner for each of those systems?
Which integrations must exist at go-live, and which can follow in a later phase?
questions.logic: The phase-1 versus phase-2 integration split is where fixed-fee SOWs most often go wrong. Get it in the customer's own words and quote it back in the scope section.

questions.text: DIDs to port: ____  ·  Toll-free numbers: ____  ·  Carriers involved: ____
Do you have current CSRs or carrier bills for all numbers?
questions.logic: Porting timelines are gated entirely on documentation the customer supplies. Anything other than "yes, all" converts to a timeline assumption rather than a task.

questions.text: Ingress and edge requirements
E911 complexity:
options: Dispatchable location per floor or room
questions.logic: Dispatchable-location-per-room is a distinct workstream with its own discovery, not a configuration checkbox. It belongs as a line item.

questions.text: Are any numbers bundled or contracted in a way that blocks porting?
Anything unusual about the number estate — main lines, hunt groups, fax, alarm circuits, elevator lines, overhead paging.
Which capabilities do you want, and when?
questions.logic: Becomes the scope baseline that the post-SOW A6.8 is measured against. The delta between what they asked for here and what they believe they bought there is a measurable trust signal — and the only way to get it is to ask the same question twice, deliberately.

questions.text: For anything marked "need to understand it first," what is your question?
questions.logic: Feeds the demo agenda, and prevents a module being quoted into a SOW that the buyer never actually understood.

questions.text: Has anyone in your organization approved AI handling customer conversations?
questions.logic: AI governance is a common late-stage blocker and it kills the highest-margin modules. "Not raised yet" on a SOW carrying virtual agent and Expert Assist means those modules should be conditional or phase-2, not phase-1.

questions.text: Call queues: ____  ·  IVR or auto-receptionist trees: ____  ·  Skills: ____  ·  Distinct call flows: ____
questions.logic: Build effort scales on flow count, not on agent count. A 40-agent center with 60 flows is a bigger build than a 300-agent center with 8.

questions.text: How complex is your routing?
Which of these apply?
How many distinct business units or brands must stay separate in the platform?
What security review will this require?
questions.logic: A schedule input, not a scope input, but it belongs in the SOW as an assumption because it sits on the critical path and you do not control it.

questions.text: What change management support do you expect from us?
Who administers the platform after go-live?
options: We expect you to manage it
questions.logic: "We expect you to manage it" is a managed-service line item, not a professional-services one. Catching that pre-proposal is the difference between a recurring revenue line and an unpriced obligation.

questions.text: Describe your approval path from here to signature.
Which approvals are still required?
Budget status:
Are you evaluating other vendors?
Target signature date.
What would stop this from happening?
Blackout periods, freeze windows and seasonal peaks.
Rank the risks most likely to delay this.
What have we not asked that will affect scope, timeline or cost?
